title: Certificates of Deposit: The Payout Account Recorded With a Bank-Owed Instruction Replacement
content:
When Piedmont Crescent Bank replaces a maturity instruction on one of its Certificates of Deposit because the instruction paid out to a closed account, the closed account cannot stay on the record either. This page governs which account is recorded in its place.

## Rule

- In place of the closed account, the record takes whichever of the owner's own checking or savings accounts the owner designates, provided that account is in active status.
- If the certificate's interest is set to be paid out rather than compounded, the account the owner names must be of the kind that interest choice pays to: a checking account where interest is paid to checking, a savings account where interest is paid to savings. The reason is that whatever account is on record when an instruction is recorded must be an active account of the owner, and the same payout account serves both the maturity instruction and the interest.
- If the certificate's interest was being paid to that very same closed account, the active account recorded with this replacement becomes the receiving account for that interest as well. The separate rule that repoints an interest payout account away from a closed account then has no application to the certificate.

## Condition, judgement, outcome (hypothetical)

| Interest choice on the certificate | Account the owner names | Acceptable as the new payout account? |
|---|---|---|
| Compounding | The owner's active checking account | Yes |
| Compounding | The owner's active savings account | Yes |
| Paid to savings | The owner's active savings account | Yes; it also receives the interest |
| Paid to savings | The owner's active checking account | No; interest paid to savings needs a savings account |
| Paid to checking | A checking account of another customer | No; it must belong to the owner |
| Paid to checking | The owner's checking account, closed | No; it must be active |

## Point of judgement

**Who picks the new account?** The owner names it; the bank's part is to see that the named account is the owner's own, is active, and is of the kind any paying-out interest choice requires.
